hero.title: Your local AI agent assets,
hero.subtitle: Berth scans the instructions, skills, MCP servers, hooks, plugins, sessions and scan sources scattered across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent — then turns them into one browsable local map.

items.title: Make assets visible
items.body: Turn plain-text skills, hooks and MCP servers from a scattered file tree into structured, connected objects.

items.title: One view across agents
items.body: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are read through separate adapters and shown in one place.

items.title: Local-first
items.body: Everything runs on your machine — zero telemetry, no cloud sync, no account required.

items.title: Read-only & safe
items.body: Berth never modifies a file. API keys and tokens are detected, never displayed.

features.heading: Your whole agent setup, at a glance

items.name: Overview
items.title: A dashboard for everything
items.body: Asset counts, recent sessions, this week's spend and health checks — all on one screen.

items.name: Sessions
items.title: Browse past work
items.body: Walk through sessions by project or date, and see the skills loaded, MCP servers connected, hooks fired and artifacts produced.

items.name: Configuration
items.title: Take inventory
items.body: Instructions and Capabilities in two columns, merged across user, project and enterprise scope, with source paths, scopes and conflicts marked.

items.name: Usage
items.title: Spend & tokens
items.body: Cost and token trends by model, project and day. Berth keeps local estimates visible without pretending to be provider billing.

items.name: Scan Engine
items.title: See the indexer itself
items.body: Settings now exposes the scan engine version, status, indexed asset count, indexed file count, errors, scheduler state and editable watcher timing.

engine.title: A visible indexer, not a hidden background task
engine.body: Berth's data layer is the standalone @berth/scan-engine package. The desktop app uses it through a worker-backed runtime, while the package also exposes a CLI and adapter API for independently maintained integrations.

metrics.label: Package
metrics.body: The scanner, adapter registry, shared asset model and CLI live in a package boundary outside the Electron UI.

metrics.label: Adapter API
metrics.body: Adapter definitions include source policy, permissions, evidence URLs, sensitivity and version probing.

metrics.label: Cache mode
metrics.body: The app restores the last local index quickly and refreshes it in the background.

metrics.label: Worker mode
metrics.body: Heavy scans run outside the renderer, with queued project-scope refreshes and file-change updates.

controls.label: Manual refresh
controls.body: Run the scanner now and watch the runtime status move from scanning back to ready.

controls.label: Watcher debounce
controls.body: Tune how long Berth waits after file changes before scheduling a refresh.

controls.label: Minimum refresh interval
controls.body: Keep noisy file watchers from repeatedly re-indexing the same project.

controls.label: Scheduler state
controls.body: See scheduled and queued refresh reasons. Pause and cancel are shown honestly as unsupported when unavailable.

adapters.title: Independent agent adapters, one asset model
adapters.body: Each adapter owns its scan roots and source policy. Shared compatibility files such as AGENTS.md can be counted as source coverage without falsely marking an agent as installed.

items.name: Claude Code
items.body: Reads instructions, skills, subagents, MCP servers, hooks, sessions and usage metadata from Claude-specific roots.

items.name: Codex
items.body: Reads Codex config, AGENTS.md, hooks, skills, sessions and rollout metadata from Codex homes and projects.

items.name: Gemini CLI
items.body: Reads settings, GEMINI.md context files, extensions and session metadata from user and project roots.

items.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
items.body: Reads Copilot instructions, agents, skills, hooks, MCP/LSP config, plugins and metadata-only session sources.

items.name: Cursor
items.body: Reads rules, MCP config, hooks, permissions, skills, agents and plugins from project and config roots.

items.name: OpenCode
items.body: Reads opencode config, agents, commands, skills, plugins, auth presence, logs and session database metadata.

items.name: OpenClaw
items.body: Reads workspace guidance, skills, extensions, plugins, session indexes, credentials presence and debug summaries.

items.name: Hermes Agent
items.body: Reads config, profiles, identity files, memories, skills, plugins, hooks and project context files.

safety.title: Readable does not mean writable
items: Berth scans known local roots and presents source paths so you can verify where each asset came from.
Credentials and tokens are treated as presence or metadata only; secret values are not displayed.
The local SQLite index and scan settings stay on this machine and are used only by Berth.
No telemetry, no account, no cloud sync. External links go to GitHub releases or cited documentation.

pages.featuresIntro: Berth turns the plain-text files and local databases behind your AI agents into structured, browsable objects. This page covers the app views, the scan engine, and the adapter model behind them.

about.intro: Berth is a local-first desktop app for people who use AI coding agents seriously enough that their local setup has become hard to see. It reads the files, indexes and session traces that shape those agents, then shows them without changing them.

sections.title: What Berth reads
sections.body: The current scanner focuses on local agent assets and the evidence needed to explain where each one came from.
items: Sessions, usage metadata and scan sources

sections.title: How the scanner is organized
sections.body: The scan engine lives in @berth/scan-engine instead of inside the UI. That package owns the shared asset model, adapter registry, CLI and adapter API.
items: Adapter v1 contracts for new agents

sections.title: What Berth does not do
sections.body: Berth is an inspector, not an editor. It avoids write operations, account systems and remote telemetry so local agent configuration can be reviewed safely.

privacy.intro: Berth is designed around local inspection. The app reads known local agent locations, stores its own local index, and does not send telemetry or require an account.

sections.title: Local files Berth reads
sections.body: The scanner looks for agent configuration, instructions, skills, hooks, plugins, MCP settings, sessions and usage metadata under known user and project roots.
items: User-level roots such as ~/.claude, ~/.codex and tool-specific homes
Project roots such as AGENTS.md, .cursor and opencode configuration
Session and usage stores when the adapter can read them safely

sections.title: Data stored by Berth
sections.body: Berth keeps a local SQLite index and local scan settings so the UI can open quickly and refresh in the background.
items: Watcher debounce and minimum refresh interval settings

sections.title: Credentials and secrets
sections.body: Adapters may detect that a credential, token or auth file exists, but Berth treats that as status metadata and does not display secret values.
items: Sensitive files are read only when an adapter declares the source policy

sections.title: Network behavior
sections.body: The app has no telemetry, account login or cloud sync. External links in the website and app point to GitHub releases or cited documentation.
items: No automatic upload of local configuration
